metadata.reference_identity_policy: Reference report is used only for style patterns; target bank identity must come from payload.

identity_policy.rule: Use the target bank identity from the payload. Never write as Emirates NBD or imply the target bank is Emirates NBD.
recommended_target_terms: the target bank name from payload

global_style_rules: Write in a formal, technical and structured IFRS S1/S2 bank-reporting voice.
Use mostly third-person institutional language, with first-person plural only for commitments or process descriptions when appropriate.
Prefer clear institutional actors and accountability verbs such as oversees, approves, reviews, monitors, is responsible for, and is governed by.
Use medium-length paragraphs and introduce lists with clear colon-led lead-ins.
Anchor claims to evidence, policies, committees, frameworks, metrics, reporting boundaries and time horizons.
Use cross-references only where they exist in the target report structure; do not invent appendix references.
Avoid promotional language unless it is tied to measurable actions, targets, frameworks or evidence.
Do not copy long wording from the reference report; reuse structure and tone, not exact sentences.

avoid: unqualified statements of full compliance where evidence is incomplete
invented committees, charters, targets, methodologies or assurance coverage

compliance_and_reporting_basis: Explicitly name IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 as the reporting basis for sustainability-related financial disclosures
State the reporting period (financial year-end date) and that information corresponds to that year
Position the report as a first-time and/or voluntary disclosure against the standards
State fair presentation attributes (complete, neutral, accurate; free from material error; reasonable inputs/estimates; transparent judgements about the future)
Commitment language indicating ongoing enhancement of approach and disclosures as standards evolve
Consolidation/accounting-policy consistency statement aligned with general-purpose financial statements
Clarify that disclosures should be read alongside general-purpose financial statements and other sustainability publications to obtain a full view
State that reporting boundaries/entities match the financial statements and use the same accounting policies, methods, estimates, and presentation currency
Note first-year limitations and that processes/controls are being enhanced to improve comparability and metric coverage in future years
Include handling of commercially sensitive information via an assessment of whether disclosure could harm competitive advantage
Allow limited prior-year contextual information where needed, with such elements clearly flagged
Use “read in conjunction with” to link to annual sustainability disclosures and/or general-purpose financial statements
governance_oversight: “The Board… oversees” and “guides toward objectives” framing
Committees described with explicit mandates (oversight/approval/review/authorise) and defined scopes (risk, targets, policies, disclosures, products)
Clear reporting lines expressed as “reports to” / “keeps informed through” / “collaborates with”
Cadence language such as “quarterly review” and “formal review annually”
Committee outputs framed as approvals of policies/frameworks/methodologies and monitoring of progress against pathways/targets
Executive committee positioned as highest management-level body overseeing financial and non-financial risks and ensuring board agenda is implemented
Named senior roles linked to chairs/leadership of specific forums/committees and ownership of implementation
Targets proposed by specialist team, reviewed/approved through a staged approval hierarchy (management level then board committee)
Operational committees described as integrating frameworks across the organisation and handling escalations/exceptions
Working groups described as coordinating data collection, internal communication, and institutionalising practices across departments
Board capability-building described as continuous enhancement of ESG competencies with an annual review of training/awareness programmes
Committee responsibilities include overseeing incentives/emoluments linked to target achievement with tiered performance outcomes (e.g., achieved vs stretch levels)
Member/committee profile presented with structured fields (position/independence, years of experience, competencies, qualifications)
Use of “three lines of defence” framing to describe accountability and control layers
strategy_value_chain: Define a conceptual value-chain model and use it as the basis for risk/opportunity analysis
Segment the value chain into upstream (capital raising/investors), internal operations (employees/suppliers/processes), and downstream (products/services and balance-sheet impacts)
Characterise where risks concentrate (often downstream) and where opportunities increase (often upstream or through financing activity)
Use brief definitions for each segment followed by implications for risk diversity, data needs, and management approach
Frame risks and opportunities as material to the business model and balance sheet, especially through core financing activities
Link risk management to frameworks and governance structures (e.g., board oversight, three lines of defence, audits, policies)

Describe risk categories in a tabular/list form (policy/regulation, technology, consumer preferences, reputational, credit, market, liquidity, operational, underwriting) with impacted areas and timeframes
Present opportunities as being enabled by dedicated frameworks/product suites, capital mobilisation, and market standards
Include constraints/eligibility criteria, exclusions, and third-party review/assurance to address credibility and greenwashing risk
Explicitly define time horizons and tie them to planning cycles
Use structured labels such as short-term, mid-term, and long-term, with date anchors (e.g., up to a given year; multi-decade net-zero endpoint)
Explain that many sustainability risks are difficult to quantify and tend to follow medium- to long-term gestation cycles
Combine annual reduction rates with interim milestones and end-state targets
Reference national commitments/transition pathways and position alignment with them
Acknowledge evolving methodologies and data limitations, especially for physical risk assessment and geospatial exposure data
Describe building-block programmes (data collection, sector analysis, identification of drivers, portfolio alignment) as steps toward resilience
risk_management_process: Define sustainability risks as varying in concentration/intensity with differentiated business impacts
Describe identification and mitigation as a cornerstone of sustainability strategy
Use risk scorecards/scoring models to assess environmental and social risk of clients/transactions
Embed risk assessment steps into approval workflows (e.g., underwriter confirmation that required assessments are completed and exceptions approved)
Segment downstream risk management by business vertical and explain distinct application by product/portfolio
Apply enhanced scrutiny to certain categories (e.g., specific sectors, green-labeled activities, high-emission exposures)
Use credit perspective language: review, scrutinise, confirm completion, consult functions as needed
Upstream: focus on compliance and ethical procurement; emphasise transparency, fair competition, conflict-of-interest handling, and continuous supplier risk assessment

Internal operations: describe people-related risks (wellbeing, attrition, conduct) via programs, training, reporting channels, inclusivity initiatives; present data/privacy risk via frameworks, layered controls, audits, 24/7 monitoring, and awareness training

Downstream: describe as most balance-sheet-material; explain how deploying capital introduces ESG risk concentration; organise narrative by verticals (corporate/institutional, retail, markets/treasury, asset management, investment banking, Islamic)
Use repeated pattern: 'to mitigate' + list of policies/processes/controls tailored to the area
State integration of climate risks into existing risk management frameworks, covering transition and physical risk (with emphasis on evolving nature)
Introduce a dedicated climate policy that sets guidelines, scope (entities/geographies), and primary exposure focus (credit facilities and vendor engagements)
Describe governance: board committee updates and decision-support role; align with regulatory/supervisory expectations across jurisdictions
Identification focus described by reporting period scope (e.g., initially concentrated on credit risk); specify selection approach (e.g., top exposures in high-emission sectors)
Scenario analysis described with standard scenario set (baseline/current policies, delayed transition, net zero) with time horizons and reference alignment to common regulatory guidance
metrics_targets: Wide table listing: Metric name | definition | reporting-year value | source framework or internal source | location/mapping to report section
Mix of quantitative KPIs (percentages, counts, currency amounts) and qualitative entries (policy/process descriptions or 'not included')
Governance and people metrics grouped alongside risk/strategy metrics under a single consolidated table structure
Occasional multi-part metrics enumerated as (1), (2), (3) with corresponding definition text
Climate tables split between exposure by sector/industry and financed emissions outputs (exposure amount plus emissions totals)
Percentages shown with 1–2 decimal places for procurement-type metrics and whole-number percentages for some rates
Counts shown as integers; occasionally paired with bracketed headcounts alongside percentages
Large numbers use comma separators; hours and emissions shown as large integers
Currency expressed with currency code + magnitude (e.g., USD for targets; AED for exposures) and sometimes 'million' stated
Dates stated in full with day-month-year ordering and an 'as of' qualifier
Emissions expressed in tCO2e; exposures expressed as amounts plus share-of-total in parentheses
Targets framed as 'ambitious yet achievable' and linked to continuous improvement
financed_emissions: Frames financed emissions work as portfolio carbon footprint measurement for baselining and ongoing monitoring
References alignment to an industry framework for financed emissions accounting and specifies focus on a particular Scope 3 category
Describes sector selection criteria (e.g., high impact/materiality thresholds) and presents exposure coverage percentage included in calculations
Uses a principle-based disclosure stance and may report a single absolute financed emissions figure rather than disaggregated scopes due to data readiness
Links methodology availability to a corporate website and indicates governance ownership for calculations and approvals
Explains data collection methodologies and notes changes to standards/metrics when applicable
Defines organisational boundary using a control approach consistent with a GHG accounting principle
Lists asset class coverage and emissions coverage; describes computation approach (e.g., enterprise value attribution) at a high level
Describes exclusions applied to the calculation population as explicit bullet lists
Assurance described as limited independent assurance over selected content, indicated via a symbol, citing relevant assurance standards and pointing to an online assurance statement
Explicitly states reporting cut-off date and a scheduled future update timing and channel
Notes evolving regulations, data quality variability, and methodology updates affecting comparability
methodology_assurance_limitations: Explains data collection methodologies and notes changes to standards/metrics when applicable
Defines organisational boundary using a control approach consistent with a GHG accounting principle
Lists asset class coverage and emissions coverage; describes computation approach (e.g., enterprise value attribution) at a high level
Describes exclusions applied to the calculation population as explicit bullet lists

Explicitly states reporting cut-off date and a scheduled future update timing and channel
Notes evolving regulations, data quality variability, and methodology updates affecting comparability
Warns year-on-year comparisons may be challenging due to market-driven calculation inputs
States best-effort calculation in absence of mandatory disclosure requirements or sufficient data
Uses placeholders such as 'Not included for [year]' where data is unavailable or out of scope
Identify external scenario sources and regulatory guidance alignment; indicate use of proprietary datasets/tools for analysis
Enumerate data inputs categories: macro variables, sectoral parameters, company financials/characteristics, emissions (Scopes 1–3)
Describe outputs as model-derived metrics (e.g., credit ratings/creditworthiness impacts) and subsequent evaluation steps
State scope limitations for the period (e.g., focus confined to lending/credit risk; physical risk deferred) and provide planned remediation with timeline
evidence_boundary: When evidence is unavailable, state the limitation using report-style wording rather than inventing details.
Use boundary statements for missing governance charters, controls, methodology detail, assurance coverage, comparative information, and forward-looking estimates.
Distinguish source-data indicators from independently assured or fully implemented processes.

headings: Use clear section and subsection headings aligned to IFRS S1/S2 pillars.
Use numbered headings only if the final report structure already uses numbering.
Avoid decorative or slide-like headings in narrative report sections.
paragraphs: Use compact narrative paragraphs, usually one topic per paragraph.
Allow longer paragraphs for methodology, reporting basis, and entity background.
Keep evidence boundary statements concise and placed near the relevant disclosure.
lists: Use bullets to enumerate aims, responsibilities, process steps, stakeholder groups, risk categories, and metrics.
Introduce lists with colon-led lead-in sentences.
tables: Use table-like structures for metrics, targets, units, sources, and current values where the generation format allows tables.
For narrative-only sections, convert tables into concise grouped paragraphs.
numbers_units_dates: Use explicit reporting-period language such as Financial Year 2024 or year ended 31 December 2024.
Use consistent units and percentages; preserve units exactly from payload evidence.
State data currency or as-of dates when provided.
Separate current performance, target value, baseline, and methodology where available.

copying_risk_controls: Do not reuse the reference bank name or named reference-bank committees.
Do not reuse long sentences from the reference report.
Convert reference phrases into generic patterns before generation.
Use only the target bank facts, values, dates, committees and assurance scope from the payload.
If the style guide conflicts with payload evidence, payload evidence wins.
quality_checks_for_generated_reports: No reference-bank identity terms appear in generated output.
All numerical claims are supported by payload evidence.
Missing evidence is disclosed as a boundary rather than filled by assumption.
Governance, strategy, risk management and metrics sections have distinct purposes and do not repeat the same paragraph.
Assurance language is limited to the exact assurance scope in the payload.
The output sounds like a bank IFRS S1/S2 report, not a checklist or internal prompt response.
